title: Dimension at a point of a finite type affine scheme from its irreducible components
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $S$ be a finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], let $X=\operatorname{Spec}S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $x\in X$ correspond to a prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset S$. Then the Krull dimension of $X$ at $x$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] equals the maximum of the Krull dimensions [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] of the irreducible components of $X$ which contain $x$. Equivalently, if $\mathfrak q_1,\dots,\mathfrak q_t$ are the minimal prime ideals of $S$ contained in $\mathfrak p$, then $$\dim_xX=\max_{1\le i\le t}\dim(S/\mathfrak q_i),$$ where the right hand side uses ring Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. It also equals the minimum of $\dim(S_{\mathfrak m})$ over maximal ideals $\mathfrak m\supseteq\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].
